_: Chrome-tanned bovine / ovine leather as a thick fibrous sheet: garment nappa (0.6-1.0 mm, soft, aniline or lightly pigmented) and upholstery (0.9-1.4 mm, pigmented, top-coated). A collagen fibre network densest at the grain (outer) layer; bends like a thick plate with a soft core, stretches 30-80 % before break. No measured leather data was retrieved this session: E throughout, which is the group's biggest gap.
variants_note: suede / nubuck: the flesh side or buffed grain, matte (alpha ~0.9), absorbs water and oil readily, darkens strongly wet.

n.src: E: recalled from textbook / trade ranges, not re-read: polyurethane / acrylic topcoat ~1.48-1.52 (recalled); collagen ~1.5

sheen.v: soft broad gloss on the grain; follows the grain pattern (pores, creases); creased elbows / seat folds break the highlight

wet_darkening.v: aniline and suede darken strongly and stain (water lines); top-coated leather beads water and barely changes
wet_darkening.src: qualitative; same film physics as LEKNER88 where the surface is open

static.src: E: recalled from Marks' Handbook (MARKS), not re-read: finished leather on itself / on cloth; not measured. Against oak see the pairs file (MARKS)

surface_energy_mJ_m2.src: E: recalled from textbook / trade ranges, not re-read: PU / acrylic topcoat (recalled)

tack.v: smooth finished leather sticks to sweaty skin (the 'leather seat in summer' peel)
tack.src: qualitative: occlusive surface + sweat film, see pairs

water_contact_angle_deg.src: E: recalled from textbook / trade ranges, not re-read: finish-dependent (recalled)

moisture_regain_pct.src: linear between FLOWERS15 measured 13.4 +/- 2.4 % at ~45 % RH and 24.2 +/- 5.0 % at 76 % RH (chrome leather, dry basis) -> 65 % RH; replaced 11-07 ~23:25 the recalled [14, 18] (E) after proof T4a

water_absorption.src: E: recalled from textbook / trade ranges, not re-read: uncoated vs coated; recalled ranges

hardness.src: not measured; soft garment leather low end

abrasion.src: TYPICAL upholstery leather rating band; garment nappa far lower

contact_stiffness_kPa_per_mm.src: through-thickness modulus ~1 / 2 MPa (E: compact collagen network, far stiffer than cloth pile) / thickness

compressible_to_fraction.src: leather compresses little under a seated load; upholstery foam beneath takes the deflection

restitution.src: thick sheet: a little rebound, mostly damped (not measured)

response_time_ms.src: a slap on leather is a sharper crack than on cloth (stiffer, heavier sheet)

wave_speed_m_s.src: sqrt(stretch / mass), sqrt(shear / mass) for garment leather (sim block)

deform.model_note: a thick shell: membrane + plate bending with a soft core; for sims use cloth with the bending from E t^3/12 and reduce it by the soft-core factor below

density_kg_m3.src: E: recalled from textbook / trade ranges, not re-read: apparent density of finished leather ~0.8-1.0 g/cm3 (recalled; a search summary gives the same unverified range)

E_MPa.src: E: recalled from textbook / trade ranges, not re-read: recalled order of magnitude; strongly sample- and direction-dependent (the cited search confirms the dependence on animal, site and direction)

strength_kPa.src: E: recalled from textbook / trade ranges, not re-read: tensile strength 15-30 N/mm2 (recalled typical spec band, ISO 3376 method)

elongation_at_break_pct.src: E: recalled from textbook / trade ranges, not re-read: recalled

tear_N.src: E: recalled from textbook / trade ranges, not re-read: recalled spec bands

drape_coefficient_pct.src: stiff end of the Cusick scale

recovery.v: viscoelastic; creases at flex points (elbows, seat) become permanent 'break' lines; stretch-in-use (bagging) is permanent

sim._: Shell: stretch from E t; bending from the soft-core plate value; damp heavily (leather creaks, little rebound).

stretch_N_m.src: E t: 10 MPa x 0.8 mm, 20 MPa x 1.2 mm (both E)

conductivity_W_mK.src: E: recalled from textbook / trade ranges, not re-read: leather ~0.12-0.18 (recalled)

heat_capacity_J_kgK.src: E: recalled from textbook / trade ranges, not re-read: recalled

effusivity.src: sqrt(0.15 x 850 x 1500): warmer to touch than metal, cooler than wool cloth

shrink_temperature_C.src: E: recalled from textbook / trade ranges, not re-read: chrome-tanned leather shrinks above ~100 C wet (recalled)

wet.src: wet leather is softer and stretches more; dried without oiling it stiffens and can crack (fat-liquor washed out)

warm_body_contact.src: upholstery under skin warms and the sweat film raises friction and tack (pairs)

LEKNER88.cite: Lekner J, Dorf MC. Why some things are darker when wet. Appl Opt 27(7):1278-1280 (1988): a water film's total internal reflection returns diffuse light to an absorbing surface for another chance of absorption (Angstrom), plus a lower relative index inside
LEKNER88.lic: paywalled journal; author copy; formula used, text studied only

MARKS.cite: Marks' Standard Handbook for Mechanical Engineers, friction table: leather on oak static 0.61, sliding 0.52 (parallel to grain). Recalled, not re-opened

TYPICAL.cite: Trade and textbook typical values (fabric weight classes, Martindale rating bands such as EN 14465 upholstery 'heavy domestic' >= 25 000 rubs, fabric emissivity ~0.9, effective fabric conductivity dominated by trapped air 0.03-0.06 W/mK). Used only where no measured value was retrieved; each use says why
